text:
support_sam: Heads-up — customer X (EU region) reporting repeated 503s from hosted inference for ~30m. Example request_id=0a1b2c3. They see timeouts then retries. Escalating to incidents.
deploy-bot: ALERT hosted-gateway:eu-west:503-spike fired (37m ago). 5m avg 503 rate = 12.5% (threshold 2%)
raj: I'm on infra. Node-level OOMs? K8s shows several pod restarts in inference-proxy-eu-1/2. Restart counts + conn-sockets peaked around the same time as alerts.
sofia: Autoscaler reports: min_replicas=2, current=2, target=7 but couldn't scale fast enough due to controller cooldown. Traffic fanout from a few heavy customers spiked. Suggest bump min to 5 while we triage.
liam: Also seeing KV cache stall on the proxy side — miss rate jumped ~4x, and we have a backlog of cold KV loads saturating CPU. Could be the recent cache warmup tweak in Canary.
diane: I want to try rolling back the cache warmup change in Canary -> prod path. That change changed prefix eviction heuristics. If cache churn is the culprit, rollback should reduce backend pressure quickly.
ops_bot: Runbook — Gateway 5xx triage: https://go/runbooks/gateway-5xx. Quick mitigation commands:
```
# scale replicas
kubectl scale deployment inference-proxy-eu --replicas=5 -n hosted

# flush KV prefix for heavy customers (careful)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://kv-internal/eu/flush?prefix=customerX
```
raj: I'm going to scale to 5 now and watch. If backpressure drops we can avoid full rollback. Starting scale at 6329004387.
support_sam: I'll send a short customer update: "We're investigating elevated 5xxs in eu-west. We've applied mitigations and will update in ~20m. Apologies for the disruption." Any additions?
liam: Add: "Requests are being routed to additional proxy capacity; engineering is investigating a cache-related regression." Keeps them informed but not too deep.
diane: Scale looks to be partially effective — 503 rate dropped from ~12% to ~6% in last 2m. But some customers still hitting retries. I'll queue rollback of warmup change if rates don't fall further.
sofia: Also opened a quick autoscaler policy change PR to bump min_replicas for eu-west and shorten cooldown. Link: https://go/pull/1138
ops_bot: NOTE: After manual scale & partial rollback hold, we've enabled a short-term circuit breaker for heavy-fanout customers (rate-limit to 50rps per client) at 6329004520.
support_sam: Customer updated at 6329004605 with the mitigation note. They replied: "Thanks — we're seeing improvement but still occasional 503s. Will monitor."
raj: Follow-up checks: connection pool usage normalizing, CPU on proxy dims down, KV load decreased after partial rollback metric tweak. I think two root causes: cache churn + insufficient min replicas for bursty fanout.
diane: ACTIONS (immediate):
- ACTION: Complete rollback of cache warmup change if numbers don't improve in 10m - owner: diane - ETA: +15m
- ACTION: Merge autoscaler policy change (bump min to 5, shorten cooldown) - owner: sofia - ETA: +30m
- ACTION: Add granular monitoring for per-customer fanout and add alert for spike > 100x baseline - owner: raj - ETA: 3d
- ACTION: Postmortem + JIRA with RCA and mitigation plan - owner: liam - ETA: 1d
sofia: I'll also add a quick customer-level quota to avoid head-of-line impact across tenants. Will coordinate with billing team if needed.
support_sam: I'll follow up with the customer with the list of mitigations and ETA for postmortem. Drafted message pinned to thread.
diane: Post-incident note: once stable, we should run a canary test simulating heavy fanout patterns and KV churn. Add to Optimize playbook.
liam: Agreed. Ending active war room; will re-open if 503 rate > 3% sustained. Creating postmortem ticket now (PM-7654).
ops_bot: war-room closed by raj at 6329005401 — metrics stable and customer acknowledged improvement.
